prompt: Which publication tells the users 'what to do' for the operation of a particular communications system?
explanation: Page 9 says the CEOI is a combat order with specific instructions for the operation of a particular communications system and tells the users what to do.

prompt: Which publication tells the users 'how to do it' for the items included in the CEOI?
explanation: Page 9 says the CESI contains instructions explaining the use of the items included in the CEOI and tells the users how to do it.

prompt: The CESI at all echelons of command is:
options: Prepared for short periods and subject to frequent change
explanation: Page 12 says the CESI at all echelons of command is identical or similar in contents and is permanent in nature, while the CEOI is subject to frequent change.

prompt: Which of the following is a similarity between the CEOI and the CESI?
options: Both are prepared in four editions
Both are prepared for short periods and subject to frequent change
Both tell the users what to do
Both are divided into 7 or 8 distinct sections
explanation: Page 13 lists as similarities that both are divided into 7 or 8 distinct sections, share an identical format, and have identical instructions prepared by the highest commands.

prompt: Communication is the responsibility of the:
explanation: Page 14 says communication is the responsibility of the commander; the signal officer is responsible to him for technical control and staff supervision.

prompt: The signal officer is responsible to his commander for which of the following?
options: Technical control and staff supervision over all communications-electronics activities of the command
The preparation and issuance of the CEOI only, but not the CESI
Overall responsibility for communications, in place of the commander
The authentication of every message sent over the command's nets
explanation: Page 14 says the signal officer is responsible for the preparation and issuance of both the CESI and CEOI, and to his commander for technical control and staff supervision of all communications-electronics activities.

prompt: A copy number is assigned to each published copy of the CEOI and CESI to facilitate:
explanation: Page 15 says each copy published is assigned a copy number to facilitate distribution, control and accounting.

prompt: The short title assigned to the CEOI and CESI identifies a:
explanation: Page 16 says the short title identifies a particular edition of the CESI or CEOI.

prompt: Which CEOI edition is the basic edition that is in effect?
explanation: Pages 21 and 22 describe the 1st edition as the basic edition, the effective one; the 2nd edition is the first reserve and is not in effect.

prompt: The CEOI is prepared in four editions in order to:
options: Provide a separate edition for each echelon of command
Reduce the number of copies needed in each unit
Facilitate replacement in the event of a compromise
Allow frequent change of its general section
explanation: Page 26 says the CEOI is prepared in four editions in order to facilitate replacement in the event of a compromise.

prompt: In case of compromise, the first reserve or second edition is:
options: Pulled out of circulation with the compromised edition
Kept in the issuing headquarters until the third reserve is issued
Upgraded into the first or basic edition
Stored in the same place as the compromised edition
explanation: Page 26 says that in case of compromise, the document is pulled out of circulation and the first reserve is upgraded into the first or basic edition.

prompt: Which of the following situations makes a CEOI or CESI compromised?
options: The document is replaced by a new edition on schedule
The document is believed to have been exposed to unauthorized personnel
The document is returned to the issuing headquarters after use
Only extracts of its items are taken forward to the command post
explanation: Page 17 says compromise exists when the document is known or believed to have been captured, lost or exposed to unauthorized personnel, or misused. Page 19 allows extracts to be taken to the command post.

prompt: Which two types of report are made when a compromise occurs?
options: Preliminary report and final inventory report
explanation: Page 18 lists the types of report as the immediate report (spot report) and the subsequent written report.

prompt: Which of the following is contained in the immediate report of a compromise?
options: Date and time of the compromise
explanation: Page 18 says the immediate report gives the short title or item numbers of the compromised material and the date and time of compromise. The other items belong to the subsequent written report.

prompt: The Authentication Section protects the communication system from:
options: Compromise of the code and cipher items
Loss of the first reserve edition
explanation: Page 33 says the Authentication Section (items 20-29) holds the type of authentication used to protect the communication system from fraudulent reception or transmission.

prompt: Which of the following is NOT a mandatory item of the General Section?
explanation: Page 28 lists the index, distribution and general information as the mandatory items of the General Section. The Messenger Section is a separate section (page 32).

prompt: Which General Section item contains the titles of the items, the numbers corresponding to the titles, and the effective date of each item?
explanation: Page 29 says the index contains the titles of the items in the CESI/CEOI, the corresponding numbers and the effective date of each item.

prompt: It is the General Section item that specifies the units to receive copies, including the number of copies each.
explanation: Page 30 says the distribution item specifies the units to receive copies of the CESI and items of the CEOI, including the number of copies each.

prompt: In an item number, the number before the hyphen identifies the specific item and is never changed for the same item. What is it called?
explanation: Page 41 says the base number appears before the hyphen, identifies the specific item and is never changed for the same item.

prompt: The entire CEOI/CESI is authenticated for the commander only in which item?
explanation: Page 47 says it is only in the index item that the entire CEOI/CESI is authenticated for the commander, to indicate that the order is valid and issued by, or for, the commander.
